COMMENCE AT 7:00 PM.

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, and proposed Resolution No. 2521, due to the continuing
  state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of the
  COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may
  participate in-person in the Council Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling 1-669-900-6833 from any phone, Meeting
  ID: 861 5070 6052, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using
  the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 861 5070 6052, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 23, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:03 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), due to the continuing state
of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of
the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by the following members of the Lion’s Heart Organization: Nicholas Oreb, Bensen
Webster, Michael Oreb and Moses Newmark.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada

4.  CEREMONIAL

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-I AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF AUGUST 2022

  APPROVED WARRANTS 65359 THROUGH 65412 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $606,832.95; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080122 THROUGH
  080522 IN THE AMOUNT OF $188,158.38; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $794,991.33 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF JULY 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
AUGUST 23, 2022
 D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF JULY 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF JULY 26, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF JULY 18, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 15, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS BOARD MEETING
  HIGHLIGHTS OF JUNE 23, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE THE CONTINUED USE OF
  TELECONFERENCE ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC
  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION 2521 TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  CONTINUE TO IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE TELECONFERENCE
  ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS
  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF FREE
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE – THIRD QUARTER 2022

Waste Management Representative Erick Quintero presented a virtual drawing for one year of
free service for a residential customer and announced the commercial customer winner.

  RESIDENTIAL WINNER: 114 Cottonwood Circle
  COMMERCIAL WINNER: Calvary Chapel, 735 Silver Spur Rd

B.  DROUGHT AND WATER RESTRICTIONS VERBAL REPORT: WEST BASIN
  MUNICIPAL WATER DISTRICT, WATER REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT,
  METROPOLITAN WATER DISTRICT OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA, CALIFORNIA
  WATER SERVICE

Updates on current drought and water restrictions provided by the following representatives
from each agency:

  -  West Basin Municipal Water District: Harold Williams, Division I Board of Director
  and E.J. Caldwell, Policy & Resources Development Department Manager
  -  Metropolitan Water District of Southern California: Charles Gale, Government Affairs
  Liaison
  -  Water Replenishment District: Rob Katherman, Director
  -  California Water Service: Agustin Baeza, Palos Verdes Peninsula Operations
  Manager and Tammie Myers, Conservation Coordinator

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220255. A PRECISE PLAN OF DESIGN (PPD)
  FOR GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT PROJECT (CITY
  COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 2523) & INITIAL STUDY WITH PROPOSED
  MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION (ISMND) UNDER THE CALIFORNIA

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 23, 2022
   ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) (CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO.
  2522).
  LOCATION: SOUTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH & PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST (27305 PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST).
  APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1.) Open the Public Hearing; 2.) Take Public
  Testimony; 3.) Discuss the Project; 4.) Close the Public Hearing; and 5.) Approve the
  Project by Adopting Resolution Nos. 2522 (ISMND) and 2523 (PPD).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN confirmed that certain traffic maneuvers were
considered when exiting onto Palos Verdes Drive East, and confirmed additional space will
be made to allow for pedestrians to safely walk since there is no formal sidewalk.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba reported on the recent meetings
held with staff, the Subcommittee and the Palos Verdes Land Conservancy to ensure all
issues are addressed. Removal of the Land Conservancy’s offices, inclusion of the outdoor
classroom, storage rooms and shade coverings were among the items discussed.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she was glad the bus pull-out area was
eliminated.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that the Land
Conservancy’s offices were no longer able to be located at the Nature Center, due to space
limitations, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2522.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2522 by title.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2523.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2523 by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 23, 2022
 **ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

The City Council presented a Certificate of Recognition to the League of Women Voters of
Palos Verdes Peninsula, in recognition of the upcoming 102nd Anniversary of the certification
of the 19th Amendment, which gave American women the right to vote, also known as
Women’s Equality Day, on August 26, 2022. The certificate was accepted by co-presidents
Janet MacLeod and Linda Herman.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  NOVEMBER 8, 2022 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2524 canceling the
  November 8, 2022 election and appointing Britt Huff and Pam Brown Schachter each
  to four-year terms of office as Council Members.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2524 CANCELING THE NOVEMBER 8, 2022
  ELECTION AND APPOINTING BRITT HUFF AND PAM BROWN
  SCHACHTER EACH TO FOUR-YEAR TERMS OF OFFICE AS COUNCIL
  MEMBERS.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2524 by title.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN congratulated Council Member-Elect Pam Brown Schachter on her
appointment. He also noted that this will be the first time in the City’s history where four
women serve on the City Council. He also noted that COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN
will have served five terms as Mayor and will be the longest serving City Council Member in
the City’s history, having served for 25 years at the end of his term.

B.  APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. 2520 ADOPTING THE 2017 UPDATED
  GREATER LOS ANGELES COUNTY INTEGRATED REGIONAL WATER
  MANAGEMENT PLAN

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2520 approving
  adoption of the 2017 Updated Greater Los Angeles County Region Integrated
  Regional Water Management Plan (GLAC IRWMP).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2520 APPROVING ADOPTION OF THE 2017
  UPDATED GREATER LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGION INTEGRATED
  REGIONAL WATER MANAGEMENT PLAN (GLAC IRWMP).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 23, 2022
   AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2520 by title.

C.  APPROVE A FIVE-YEAR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH HdL
  COMPANIES TO PROVIDE TAX MANAGEMENT AND INFORMATION SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1.) approve the agreement with Hinderliter,
  De Llamas and Associates (HdL) in the amount of $4,200 annually and 15% of all
  new sales for sales and use tax audit and management services. Implementation cost
  of $6,500 and $16 per processed account for business license services and 40% of
  the revenues and 25% collections received for discovery; 2.) approve the agreement
  with HdL Coren & Cone in the amount of $7,200 annually plus 25% of net tax
  revenues for property tax services; and 3.) adopt Resolution No. 2526 authorizing
  HdL to examine sales and property tax information with the California Department of
  Tax & Fee Administration (CDTFA) and Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax
  Collector.

Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Senior Accountant Estrada explained that this item is being brought to the Council in response
to unsatisfactory service provided by Avenu Insights, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
ZUCKERMAN.

City Manager Grammer explained that there is a provision that allows the City to cancel the
contract with 30 days’ notice, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that it could potentially be costly for the City if HdL
identifies a large number of sources that weren’t collected from in the past. Senior Accountant
